statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 12% remains well below the block threshold, while cross-asset stress stays extreme on crude above $100 and a 10-year yield at 2023 highs.
recommendation: Conditions are described as two-way and mean-reverting at the assessment cutoff, with the session's two largest scheduled catalysts already cleared. The narrow evidence-based danger window falls on the September 10 producer price and jobless claims release and the US cash open that immediately follows it.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds mid-range into the close as the 10-year auction and the Apple keynote clear without one-way structure
body: At the assessment cutoff cash NDX trades 29,440.37, -0.23% against the 29,507.70 previous close, essentially back at its 29,431.94 open after a 29,334.40-29,563.60 session range; NQ front-month futures are 29,460.00, -0.27% versus the 29,538.75 settle, inside a 29,333.25-29,633.75 range. Both session extremes have therefore been retraced rather than extended, which is the specific observed evidence that keeps tail risk in the low band. Two of the day's largest scheduled catalysts have now cleared without producing index-level dislocation: the 10-year note auction stopped at 4.834% against 4.683% previously at 17:00Z, and the Apple keynote under new chief executive John Ternus delivered the iPhone 18 Pro, the foldable iPhone Duo, Apple Watch Series 12 and AirPods 5, with Apple shares easing modestly rather than moving the index. Cross-asset stress by contrast remains extreme. Brent trades near $101.29, up 3.4%, and WTI near $96.39, up 3.6%, the highest since May, after US forces destroyed five Iranian crude tankers in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island and Iran struck a Jordanian base and commercial shipping, with the Strait of Hormuz still effectively closed against a standing US naval blockade. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.837% within a 4.794-4.857% day range, its highest since October 2023, the 30-year is near 5.3% and the 2-year is 4.43%, a bear-steepening that follows the Treasury's expanded buyback operation. Rate expectations have turned hawkish, with reporting placing roughly a 60% probability on a 25 basis point hike at the September 16 meeting. VIX at 16.24 is up 3.3% but off its 16.68 session high and remains historically contained, which is difficult to reconcile with a disorderly path already underway. Index internals are split rather than uniformly weak: META is up close to 7% on its Muse agent launch while most other megacaps are lower, semiconductors are mixed with AMD, MU, QCOM, ARM and INTC higher against NVDA and AVGO lower, and small caps underperform. That combination of an intact two-way range, a contained volatility surface, cleared catalysts and genuinely severe macro inputs is scored as extreme stress with low tail. The dominant mode is mixed. Shared delayed cross-asset context was older than the freshness threshold at run time and was reviewed for discovery only; it did not drive this assessment.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours were quiet through the US evening and the Asian session, with tail between 5% and 9% and stress in the high band. Stress climbed steadily through the European morning as crude cleared $100 and Treasury yields extended, and tail peaked at 20% in the 12:00Z hour on a trend-down European tape before easing back into the low-to-mid teens once the US cash session produced genuine two-way price discovery. Tail has now held at 12% to 13% for the last three published hours while stress stayed at 82%. The 10:00Z hour has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries the closing auction as its only remaining checkpoint, after which conditional tail decays toward the single-digit overnight baseline the preceding cycle actually produced. The CME reopen around 22:00Z is the thinnest liquidity window and the standing channel for a Middle East or crude gap. Conditional risk then rebuilds through the European morning into the horizon's highest reading on September 10, where the WATCH state is mapped across the 12:30Z producer price and jobless claims release and the 13:30Z US cash open that follows it. Conditional tail decays through the US morning before a secondary lift into the 17:00Z 30-year auction. No future price path, release outcome or headline is asserted anywhere in this forecast.
